Day 2 Convective Outlook  
NWS Storm Prediction Center Norman OK
1229 AM CDT Mon Aug 03 2026

Valid 041200Z - 051200Z

...THERE IS A MARGINAL RISK OF SEVERE THUNDERSTORMS IN SOUTHEAST
ARIZONA...SOUTH-CENTRAL COLORADO...NORTH-CENTRAL AND NORTHEAST NEW
MEXICO...AND PORTIONS OF THE CAROLINAS...

...SUMMARY...
Isolated severe storms capable of severe wind gusts and marginally
severe hail appear possible in southeast Arizona, south-central
Colorado, and north-central and northeast New Mexico Tuesday
afternoon and evening. Locally damaging winds may occur with
stronger storms in the Carolinas.

...Synopsis...

A broad, cyclonic flow regime is forecast from the northern Rockies
into the Great Lakes, to the north of an elongating upper high over
the Lower CO Valley into the southern Rockies. Within that pattern,
there is a model signal that a low-amplitude disturbance and
associated mid-level wind maximum will move through the northern
Plains and mid MO Valley. Elsewhere, an upper low centered over the
southern Appalachians Tuesday morning is expected to weaken while
slowly shifting north-northwest. 

At the surface, a front will move into the upper Great Lakes with
the boundary trailing southwest through the mid MO Valley into the
southern High Plains. A weak surface low may evolve along the front
over the mid or lower MO Valley Tuesday afternoon into evening. 


...Southeast Arizona...

Widely scattered thunderstorms are anticipated by mid afternoon
along the Gila Mountains and high terrain nearer to the
international border within a moderately unstable environment with
MLCAPE up to 1000-1500 J/kg. The presence of a deep, well-mixed
boundary layer will enhance evaporative cooling potential in the
sub-cloud layer with an associated risk for locally severe wind
gusts as storms advance southwest into the lower desert during the
late afternoon into evening. Some threat for marginally severe hail
may exist with the storms developing along the international border
owing to slightly stronger deep-layer shear.


...South-central Colorado and north-central and northeast New
Mexico...

A relatively small spatial corridor of modest instability and 30-35
kt of deep-layer shear is forecast to materialize in the lee of the
Sangre De Cristo Mountains Tuesday afternoon and evening. The
favored corridor extends from where the surface front intersects the
high terrain northward within the immediate post-frontal upslope.
Several of the 00Z CAMs indicate the potential for isolated to
widely scattered storms capable of a few occurrences of marginally
severe hail and/or locally severe wind gusts.


...Carolinas...

Forcing for ascent associated with the deep-layer low is expected to
contribute to an increase in thunderstorms through the day. Where
stronger heating can occur, the presence of a moist boundary layer
will support MLCAPE up to 1000-2000 J/kg. While stronger upper-level
winds are forecast within the eastern periphery of the low, vertical
shear through the lower half of the storm depth is expected to
remain relatively weak, limiting the potential for storm
organization. Nonetheless, steepening low-level lapse rates and a
high precipitable water may enhance wet microburst potential, with a
few damaging wind gusts possible.


...Middle and Lower Missouri Valley into the upper Midwest...

Consensus of the 00Z models suggests the majority of thunderstorm
activity will likely remain elevated to the north of the front in NE
and IA within a strongly sheared, but only marginally unstable
environment. Poor mid-level lapse rates are expected to limit any
severe hail threat. There is some model signal for isolated storm
development during the afternoon into evening along the front from
the lower MO Valley into southern/eastern WI. However, given that
there is considerable model variability in the degree of instability
ahead of the boundary, and that vertical shear will be somewhat
marginal across the warm sector, no probabilities will be included
in this forecast.

..Mead.. 08/03/2026

$$

Day 3 Convective Outlook  
NWS Storm Prediction Center Norman OK
0225 AM CDT Mon Aug 03 2026

Valid 051200Z - 061200Z

...THERE IS A MARGINAL RISK OF SEVERE THUNDERSTORMS FROM EASTERN
KANSAS INTO WEST-CENTRAL ILLINOIS...OVER PORTIONS OF SOUTHERN
ARIZONA...AND FROM SOUTH-CENTRAL COLORADO INTO NORTHEAST NEW
MEXICO...

...SUMMARY...
Isolated severe storms appear possible from eastern Kansas into
west-central Illinois, over portions of southern Arizona, and from
south-central Colorado into northeast New Mexico Wednesday afternoon
and evening.

...Synopsis...

A broad, cyclonic flow regime will continue from the northern
Rockies into the Great Lakes with an embedded short-wave trough and
associated mid-level jet streak moving through the mid and lower MO
Valley. At the surface, a front will move through the upper Great
Lakes with the western extension of the boundary settling more
slowly south into the mid MS Valley and the southern High Plains.


...Lower Missouri and mid Mississippi Valleys into eastern Kansas...

Thunderstorms are expected to be ongoing at 12Z Wednesday along and
to the north of the surface front from portions of NE and IA into
southern WI and northern IL. Forcing for ascent attendant to the
short-wave trough moving through the region may sustain a subset of
the early-day storms into afternoon. Associated outflow may modulate
the position of the synoptic front with lingering clouds limiting
instability in some areas. Consensus of model guidance indicates the
corridor from eastern KS into west-central IL as being the most
probable location for moderate to strong instability by afternoon.
That area will coincide with the southern fringe of stronger
deep-layer shear oriented largely parallel to the front, suggesting
the potential for at least isolated severe weather during the
afternoon through evening. Only a 5% probability contour has been
included in this forecast due to uncertainties in the specific
location of the effective surface front.  


...Southern Arizona...

Similar to previous days, diurnally enhanced thunderstorms are
expected to form over the Gila Mountains with subsequent
south/southward movement into the lower desert, where a moderately
unstable environment is expected to reside. While deep-layer shear
will remain relatively weak, the presence of a deep, well-mixed
boundary layer will support the potential for isolated severe wind
gusts during the afternoon into evening.


...South-central Colorado into northeast New Mexico...

Isolated storms appear possible Wednesday afternoon into evening
along the Sangre de Cristo Mountains and adjacent Raton Mesa within
a modestly moist, post-frontal upslope regime. The presence of steep
low/mid-level lapse rates and resultant moderate instability will
coincide with 30-40 kt of deep-layer shear, suggesting the potential
for isolated severe weather.

..Mead.. 08/03/2026

Day 4-8 Convective Outlook  
NWS Storm Prediction Center Norman OK
0329 AM CDT Mon Aug 03 2026

Valid 061200Z - 111200Z

...DISCUSSION...
...Day 4/Thursday...

Broad troughing is forecast from the northern Plains through the
Great Lakes with a series of disturbances moving through that
airflow pattern. Elsewhere, an elongated vorticity ribbon will
progress from the central and southern Appalachians into the
Northeast. At the surface, a front initially from the southern Great
Lakes into the southern Plains is forecast to weaken. Over the
eastern CONUS, southerly winds will maintain a broad corridor of 70+
F dewpoints along and east of the Appalachians, which will
contribute to moderate instability by afternoon. Aided by the
approach of the disturbance aloft, thunderstorms are expected to
increase in coverage through the afternoon with some severe weather
possible. Generally weak vertical shear and the absence of a
coherent front in the region lead to uncertainty in where the
greatest threat may materialize.

An isolated severe threat may also develop along the front from the
Ozark Plateau into the southern High Plains, and in AZ during the
afternoon and evening.  
 

...Day 5/Friday...

An intense mid/upper-level low is expected to evolve over central
Canada with upper highs situated over the Great Basin and off the
Mid-Atlantic Coast. Between those features, corridors of stronger
mid-level flow are forecast from the northern Rockies into the
northern Plains, and to a lesser extent over the Northeast.
Some severe weather threat may again materialize from the
Mid-Atlantic into southern New England in the vicinity of a surface
trough. However, the strongest vertical shear is forecast to be
displaced to the north of the stronger instability, leading to
uncertainty in the extent of the severe weather threat. Isolated
severe storms also appear possible along a front moving into the
upper MS Valley.


...Days 6-8/Saturday through Monday...

The various 00Z ensemble means indicate an upper low initially over
Hudson Bay shifting east into northern QC with persistent ridging
over the southern CONUS. Between those features, a belt of enhanced
mid-level flow is forecast across the northern tier of states with
some signal for continued troughing through Sunday over the Great
Lakes into the OH Valley. At the surface, there is ensemble member
clustering in surface low positions over the northern Plains along a
front extending into the upper Great Lakes. There is a model signal
for the front to continue into the Great Lakes and Midwest, where
some severe weather threat appears possible. A separate severe
weather risk may also persist from the Mid-Atlantic into New
England.

..Mead.. 08/03/2026

Day 1 Convective Outlook  
NWS Storm Prediction Center Norman OK
1130 AM CDT Mon Aug 03 2026

Valid 031630Z - 041200Z

...THERE IS A SLIGHT RISK OF SEVERE THUNDERSTORMS ACROSS PARTS OF
THE NORTHERN PLAINS INTO THE UPPER MIDWEST...AND SOUTHERN ARIZONA...

...SUMMARY...
Scattered severe thunderstorms are possible today into tonight
across parts of the eastern Dakotas into northern Minnesota, as well
as across portions of southern Arizona.

...Northern/Central Plains into the Upper Midwest...
Post-frontal thunderstorms occurring this morning across ND have
remained mostly sub-severe over the past couple of hours. A stout
low-level inversion noted on the observed 12Z INL sounding will
likely inhibit surface-based thunderstorms from developing until
late this afternoon or early evening across the eastern Dakotas into
northern MN. Still, gradual airmass destabilization is anticipated
across this region along/ahead of a cold front through the
afternoon. Large-scale ascent attendant to an ejecting mid-level
shortwave trough from MT into ND will eventually aid scattered
convective development along/near the front, most likely by 22-01Z.
Moderate instability coupled with strong deep-layer shear will
support some threat for supercells and large hail initially, before
upscale growth into clusters supports an increasing severe/damaging
wind threat with eastward extent into northern MN this evening. A
tornado or two may also occur as low-level shear gradually increases
in a narrow corridor ahead of the front this evening.

Isolated to widely scattered thunderstorm development is forecast
with southward extent into the central High Plains. A hot and very
well-mixed low-level airmass ahead of the front/surface trough
across this area may support occasional severe gusts with convective
outflow. But, weaker mid-level winds and related modest deep-layer
shear should result in only loosely organized clusters/cells. This
activity should weaken with the loss of daytime heating.

...Southwest...
Around 15-25 kt of east-northeasterly mid-level winds will persist
today across far southern AZ/NM, to the south of prominent upper
ridging that will remain anchored over the Southwest. Recent visible
satellite imagery shows mostly clear conditions across southeast AZ,
with latest surface observations showing ample low-level moisture
present (surface dewpoints generally in the low to mid 60s across
lower elevations). Ample heating of this moist airmass will support
moderate instability by mid afternoon. Current expectations are for
thunderstorms to initially develop over the higher terrain of
southeast AZ as convective temperatures are reached, and
subsequently spread west-southwestward into the lower deserts
through the evening. Some organization/clustering appears possible
with this activity, and the Slight Risk for severe wind gusts up to
60-75 mph has been maintained with no changes. Isolated hail may
also occur with the strongest cores that develop initially.

...Northeast/Northern Mid-Atlantic...
An upper trough with enhanced mid-level south-southwesterly flow
will advance eastward across the Northeast and northern Mid-Atlantic
today. A weak surface low should develop northward into southern
Quebec, with a trailing cold front advancing eastward across the
Northeast this afternoon/evening. Filtered daytime heating of a
seasonably very moist airmass (reference 12Z observed soundings from
OKX/ALB/GYX) will support modest MLCAPE up to 500 J/kg, even though
mid-level lapse rates remain quite poor. Thunderstorms developing
along and ahead of the cold front may pose an isolated threat for
damaging winds given the enhanced flow present at low/mid levels. A
brief tornado or two could also occur across parts of New England
where effective SRH may be locally greater in tandem with a
southerly low-level jet. Still, the overall poor thermodynamic
environment should limit a greater severe wind threat from
developing this afternoon.

..Gleason/Lyons.. 08/03/2026
